## Research Findings: Ibuprofen and COVID-19 Severity

**Origin of the claim:** This idea gained traction in March 2020 when French Health Minister Olivier Véran tweeted that ibuprofen and other NSAIDs might "aggravate" COVID-19, based on speculative mechanisms (e.g., NSAIDs upregulating ACE2 receptors, which SARS-CoV-2 uses to enter cells) rather than direct clinical evidence (https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/17/health/coronavirus-ibuprofen.html). This triggered widespread public concern and rapid media coverage (https://edition.cnn.com/2020/03/16/health/coronavirus-ibuprofen-french-health-minister-scn-intl-scli/index.html).

**Official response:** The WHO quickly clarified that there was no evidence ibuprofen worsens COVID-19 and withdrew earlier tentative cautionary language; Health Canada echoed this (https://www.cbc.ca/news/health/ibuprofen-covid-19-novel-coronavirus-1.5501496).

**Subsequent research:** Since then, multiple observational and cohort studies have specifically tested this hypothesis:
- A prescription-based cohort study found no significantly increased risk of severe COVID-19 among ibuprofen users versus non-users (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7537121/).
- A large 38-hospital study found NSAID use was *not* associated with increased severity, mortality, ventilation, or kidney injury—and some analyses even suggested lower mortality and severity among NSAID users (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9107579/, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12985-022-01813-2).
- A systematic review concluded data "did not suggest" NSAIDs increase infection risk or COVID-19 severity, though it flagged methodological limitations in existing studies (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8426976/).

**Conclusion:** The claim that ibuprofen worsens COVID-19 originated from a plausible but unproven biological hypothesis, not solid data. The best available evidence—multiple cohort studies, systematic reviews, and major health authorities (WHO, Health Canada)—does not support this claim. Current consensus is that ibuprofen is safe to use for COVID-19 symptom management.
